answer: Start with the bill, then the design. Each recruit carries a bond that burns when that recruit misbehaves, so the inviter pays for the clone it brought in. One example: a recruiter brings 20 accounts, one submits a copied payload, and the recruiter's bond for that account burns along with the account's own. Trust sits on a completed task, so a clean address with no work carries nothing. Seen through that prism, a big referral tree is a ridge of liabilities, and the nebula of easy signups pays only if every seat ships.
